_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from Gogs' documentation; no upstream egg.
name: Gogs
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Gogs is a painless, lightweight self-hosted Git service. The egg runs it with SQLite, and you finish the setup in the browser on the first visit, where you create the admin account.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Gogs: downloads Gogs from its GitHub releases, checked against GitHub's
# SHA-256, and writes a first configuration (SQLite). Repositories, the
# database and settings are never touched, and the binary is only replaced
# once the new one has arrived whole.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
# Downloads unpack in a folder in the server's (the install's /tmp is
# small), removed when the script ends.
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Gogs has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
tag=$(gh-release tag gogs/gogs "$version") || exit 1

if [ -x gogs ] && [ "$(cat .gogs-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Gogs $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Gogs $tag"
    gh-release download gogs/gogs "$tag" "gogs_${tag}_linux_${arch}.tar.gz" "$work/gogs.tar.gz"
    tar -xzf "$work/gogs.tar.gz" -C "$work" gogs/gogs
    install -m 0755 "$work/gogs/gogs" gogs.new
    mv -f gogs.new gogs
    echo "$tag" > .gogs-version
fi

mkdir -p custom/conf data/ssh log
# Host keys for Gogs' own SSH server (it would call ssh-keygen, which the
# server's image doesn't have). Made once and kept, so clients keep
# trusting the server.
[ -f data/ssh/gogs.rsa ] || openssl genrsa -traditional -out data/ssh/gogs.rsa 3072 2>/dev/null
[ -f data/ssh/gogs.ecdsa ] || openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out data/ssh/gogs.ecdsa 2>/dev/null
[ -f data/ssh/gogs.ed25519 ] || openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out data/ssh/gogs.ed25519 2>/dev/null
chmod 600 data/ssh/gogs.*

# A first configuration: SQLite, logs on the console. The owner finishes
# the setup on the first visit (admin account, site name, address), which
# Gogs then saves here. Sign-ups start closed (the setup page can open
# them). Ports, and logs on the console, are kept up to date at every start.
if [ ! -f custom/conf/app.ini ]; then
    cat > custom/conf/app.ini <<INI
BRAND_NAME = Gogs
RUN_USER = container
RUN_MODE = prod

[server]
PROTOCOL = http
HTTP_ADDR = 0.0.0.0
HTTP_PORT = ${SERVER_PORT:-3000}
APP_DATA_PATH = /home/container/data
DISABLE_SSH = ${DISABLE_SSH:-true}
START_SSH_SERVER = true
SSH_PORT = ${SSH_PORT:-2022}
SSH_LISTEN_PORT = ${SSH_PORT:-2022}

[database]
TYPE = sqlite3
PATH = /home/container/data/gogs.db

[repository]
ROOT = /home/container/repositories

[log]
MODE = console
LEVEL = Info
ROOT_PATH = /home/container/log

[auth]
DISABLE_REGISTRATION = true

[security]
INSTALL_LOCK = false
INI
    echo "Wrote a first configuration. Open the server's address to finish setting Gogs up."
fi
echo "Installed Gogs $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Gogs version to install, such as 0.14.4, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Disable SSH
variables.description: Set it to false to clone and push over SSH as well as HTTP. SSH needs its own port, added to the server first.

variables.name: SSH port
variables.description: The port Gogs' own SSH server listens on and shows in clone links, when SSH is on.
